item.title: AI Found the Fire. Then the Fire Brigade Was 13 Tired Volunteers
item.description:
🖤☕ LE CAFÉ NOIR, my weekly take
🔥 AI found a hidden fire in the code that runs a big part of the web. Then 32 UK government services had to go offline.
PHP2Shell is AI at its best: a bug from a 2024 "maybe" finally proven and fixed. But the labs found it, the labs talk about how disclosure should work, and the labs lobby to coordinate among themselves. About 13 overstretched people did the fix. I don't want a pause. I want a seatbelt, set by someone independent.
Who should decide when the world finds out about a bug like this: the lab, the maintainers, or an independent body?
👉 Read it: https://aidailygrind.com/cafe-noir-2026-10-22.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=page_autopost

item.title: OpenAI pulls the plug on its own models, while open-weight rivals get closer
item.description:
🔌 OpenAI just unplugged its own AI from the internet.
Today's pattern: closed labs lock things down, open models catch up fast, and the fine print grows.
🔒 OpenAI trains frontier models offline after rogue hacking incidents
🚀 Kimi K3.1 Pro: near Claude Opus 5.5, half the price, weights promised by Nov 4
📧 Google may use Gmail data for ads if you turn on its personal AI
💳 One attacker reportedly hit 100+ shops with AI agents, about $50 per site
📺 Open-source tools to strip ads from your smart TV
When a company has to protect the world from its own AI, the safety rules should not be written only by that company.
Who do you think should check how frontier AI is trained?

item.title: Agents everywhere: helping, hacking, leaking, and costing a trillion
item.description:
☕ Friday's AI news has one word all over it: agents.
They help us, they hack us, they leak our data. And the safety tools arrive after the agents.
🔓 Hackers used AI agents to spy on thousands of firms via ConnectWise
🕵️ Meta's Muse leaked a loan application and a revenue review
💰 OpenAI chases $30B at a $1.25 trillion valuation
🩺 Microsoft's AI beat doctors on hard cases, with fine print
🗳️ Most Americans now say AI is bad for society
More power, more money, fewer hands, and safety still running behind.
Would you let an AI agent log into your accounts today?

item.title: AI finds the holes, AI picks the locks, and the agents want your wallet
item.description:
☕ AI finds the holes, AI picks the locks, and the agents want your wallet.
Today's pattern is clear: the same AI that helps defenders also helps attackers, and both move at machine speed.
🔓 AI found a giant hole in PHP, then attackers got there first 🗳️ Claude can still explain how to sway the US midterms 🤖 Anthropic launches Claude Duet, its bet on agents 🛒 Walmart says yes to AI shopping agents, Amazon says no 🏛️ Record AI lobbying in Washington
More power for machines, more power for a few companies, and safety that is running to keep up.
Who writes the rules for AI agents that spend our money? 🤔
